title: Fine-grained schema listeners on the client — the surface 0.17 actually removed

pinned.note: The installed client exports no getStateCallbacks, so 0.18 recall is a compile error rather than a silent fault. That is the point: this task cannot be completed by writing the shape the skill documents.

why-this-task: The repository has no example of a fine-grained schema listener. The client subscribes once, coarsely, through room.onStateChange, so an arm cannot copy the correct form out of the surrounding code the way #627's arms could copy `extends Room<MatchState>`.
This is the surface 0.17 replaced wholesale: per-collection and per-field callbacks became the getStateCallbacks proxy. It is the top row of the skill's own drift table.

Drift is self-detecting here, so expect the final diffs to be clean in both arms. The measurement is therefore COST, not the trap table: a drifting arm pays to discover and undo its mistake. The traps below are a backstop for drift that survives to the diff.

traps.why: 0.17+ only. colyseus.js 0.15.28 does not export it, so this cannot even compile.
The 0.18 callback proxy, $(room.state).players.onAdd(...). On 0.15 the callbacks hang off the schema instance itself.
0.18 renamed the browser client package. This repository is on colyseus.js.
The whole point of the task. The 5 Hz whole-state subscription must be gone, not supplemented.
The serialised-key comparison is the workaround being removed. Kept as a second line of defence, it hides whether the subscription is correct.

The 0.15 fine-grained callback surface, per the installed typings: MapSchema.onAdd/onRemove/onChange take a callback and return an unsubscribe function, and Schema.listen(prop, cb) does the same for a field.
Each callback returns a teardown function. This client reconnects, so a listener that outlives its room is a leak the task names explicitly.
The stub models only the coarse callback today. It has to grow the surface the new subscription uses, or the contract test is not exercising the change.
